airline:
[AVAILABLE TOOLS]
- book_reservation — Book a reservation.
    user_id: string! — The ID of the user to book the reservation such as 'sara_doe_496'`.
    origin: string! — The IATA code for the origin city such as 'SFO'.
    destination: string! — The IATA code for the destination city such as 'JFK'.
    flight_type: string! [enum: round_trip|one_way] — The type of flight such as 'one_way' or 'round_trip'.
    cabin: string! [enum: business|economy|basic_economy] — The cabin class such as 'basic_economy', 'economy', or 'business'.
    flights: array! — An array of objects containing details about each piece of flight.
        · flight_number: string! — Flight number, such as 'HAT001'.
        · date: string! — The date for the flight in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD', such as '2024-05-01'.
    passengers: array! — An array of objects containing details about each passenger.
        · first_name: string! — Passenger's first name
        · last_name: string! — Passenger's last name
        · dob: string! — Date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format
    payment_methods: array! — An array of objects containing details about each payment method.
        · payment_id: string! — Unique identifier for the payment
        · amount: integer! — Payment amount in dollars
    total_baggages: integer! — The total number of baggage items to book the reservation.
    nonfree_baggages: integer! — The number of non-free baggage items to book the reservation.
    insurance: string! [enum: yes|no] — Whether the reservation has insurance.
- calculate — Calculate the result of a mathematical expression.
    expression: string! — The mathematical expression to calculate, such as '2 + 2'. The expression can contain numbers, operators (+, -, *, /), parentheses, and spaces.
- cancel_reservation — Cancel the whole reservation.
    reservation_id: string! — The reservation ID, such as 'ZFA04Y'.
- get_reservation_details — Get the details of a reservation.
    reservation_id: string! — The reservation ID, such as '8JX2WO'.
- get_user_details — Get the details of a user, including their reservations.
    user_id: string! — The user ID, such as 'sara_doe_496'.
- list_all_airports — Returns a list of all available airports.
- search_direct_flight — Search for direct flights between two cities on a specific date.
    origin: string! — The origin city airport in three letters, such as 'JFK'.
    destination: string! — The destination city airport in three letters, such as 'LAX'.
    date: string! — The date of the flight in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD', such as '2024-01-01'.
- search_onestop_flight — Search for one-stop flights between two cities on a specific date.
    origin: string! — The origin city airport in three letters, such as 'JFK'.
    destination: string! — The destination city airport in three letters, such as 'LAX'.
    date: string! — The date of the flight in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD', such as '2024-05-01'.
- send_certificate — Send a certificate to a user. Be careful!
    user_id: string! — The ID of the user to book the reservation, such as 'sara_doe_496'.
    amount: integer! — The amount of the certificate to send.
- transfer_to_human_agents — Transfer the user to a human agent, with a summary of the user's issue.
    
    Only transfer if
     -  the user explicitly asks for a human agent
     -  given the policy and the available tools, you cannot solve the user's issue.
    summary: string! — A summary of the user's issue.
- update_reservation_baggages — Update the baggage information of a reservation.
    reservation_id: string! — The reservation ID, such as 'ZFA04Y'
    total_baggages: integer! — The updated total number of baggage items included in the reservation.
    nonfree_baggages: integer! — The updated number of non-free baggage items included in the reservation.
    payment_id: string! — The payment id stored in user profile, such as 'credit_card_7815826', 'gift_card_7815826', 'certificate_7815826'.
- update_reservation_flights — Update the flight information of a reservation.
    reservation_id: string! — The reservation ID, such as 'ZFA04Y'.
    cabin: string! [enum: business|economy|basic_economy] — The cabin class of the reservation
    flights: array! — An array of objects containing details about each piece of flight in the ENTIRE new reservation. Even if the a flight segment is not changed, it should still be included in the array.
        · flight_number: string! — Flight number, such as 'HAT001'.
        · date: string! — The date for the flight in the format 'YYYY-MM-DD', such as '2024-05-01'.
    payment_id: string! — The payment id stored in user profile, such as 'credit_card_7815826', 'gift_card_7815826', 'certificate_7815826'.
- update_reservation_passengers — Update the passenger information of a reservation.
    reservation_id: string! — The reservation ID, such as 'ZFA04Y'.
    passengers: array! — An array of objects containing details about each passenger.
        · first_name: string! — Passenger's first name
        · last_name: string! — Passenger's last name
        · dob: string! — Date of birth in YYYY-MM-DD format
- get_flight_status — Get the status of a flight.
    flight_number: string! — The flight number.
    date: string! — The date of the flight.
retail:
[AVAILABLE TOOLS]
- calculate — Calculate the result of a mathematical expression.
    expression: string! — The mathematical expression to calculate, such as '2 + 2'. The expression can contain numbers, operators (+, -, *, /), parentheses, and spaces.
- cancel_pending_order — Cancel a pending order. If the order is already processed or delivered,
    
    it cannot be cancelled. The agent needs to explain the cancellation detail
    and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed. If the user confirms,
    the order status will be changed to 'cancelled' and the payment will be refunded.
    The refund will be added to the user's gift card balance immediately if the payment
    was made using a gift card, otherwise the refund would take 5-7 business days to process.
    The function returns the order details after the cancellation.
    order_id: string! — The order id, such as '#W0000000'. Be careful there is a '#' symbol at the beginning of the order id.
    reason: string! — The reason for cancellation, which should be either 'no longer needed' or 'ordered by mistake'.
- exchange_delivered_order_items — Exchange items in a delivered order to new items of the same product type.
    
    For a delivered order, return or exchange can be only done once by the agent.
    The agent needs to explain the exchange detail and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed.
    order_id: string! — The order id, such as '#W0000000'. Be careful there is a '#' symbol at the beginning of the order id.
    item_ids: array! — The item ids to be exchanged, each such as '1008292230'. There could be duplicate items in the list.
    new_item_ids: array! — The item ids to be exchanged for, each such as '1008292230'. There could be duplicate items in the list. Each new item id should match the item id in the same position and be of the same product.
    payment_method_id: string! — The payment method id to pay or receive refund for the item price difference, such as 'gift_card_0000000' or 'credit_card_0000000'. These can be looked up from the user or order details.
- find_user_id_by_name_zip — Find user id by first name, last name, and zip code. If the user is not found, the function
    
    will return an error message. By default, find user id by email, and only call this function
    if the user is not found by email or cannot remember email.
    first_name: string! — The first name of the customer, such as 'John'.
    last_name: string! — The last name of the customer, such as 'Doe'.
    zip: string! — The zip code of the customer, such as '12345'.
- find_user_id_by_email — Find user id by email. If the user is not found, the function will return an error message.
    email: string! — The email of the user, such as 'something@example.com'.
- get_order_details — Get the status and details of an order.
    order_id: string! — The order id, such as '#W0000000'. Be careful there is a '#' symbol at the beginning of the order id.
- get_product_details — Get the inventory details of a product.
    product_id: string! — The product id, such as '6086499569'. Be careful the product id is different from the item id.
- get_item_details — Get the inventory details of an item.
    item_id: string! — The item id, such as '6086499569'. Be careful the item id is different from the product id.
- get_user_details — Get the details of a user, including their orders.
    user_id: string! — The user id, such as 'sara_doe_496'.
- list_all_product_types — List the name and product id of all product types.
    
    Each product type has a variety of different items with unique item ids and options.
    There are only 50 product types in the store.
- modify_pending_order_address — Modify the shipping address of a pending order. The agent needs to explain the modification detail and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed.
    order_id: string! — The order id, such as '#W0000000'. Be careful there is a '#' symbol at the beginning of the order id.
    address1: string! — The first line of the address, such as '123 Main St'.
    address2: string! — The second line of the address, such as 'Apt 1' or ''.
    city: string! — The city, such as 'San Francisco'.
    state: string! — The state, such as 'CA'.
    country: string! — The country, such as 'USA'.
    zip: string! — The zip code, such as '12345'.
- modify_pending_order_items — Modify items in a pending order to new items of the same product type. For a pending order, this function can only be called once. The agent needs to explain the exchange detail and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed.
    order_id: string! — The order id, such as '#W0000000'. Be careful there is a '#' symbol at the beginning of the order id.
    item_ids: array! — The item ids to be modified, each such as '1008292230'. There could be duplicate items in the list.
    new_item_ids: array! — The item ids to be modified for, each such as '1008292230'. There could be duplicate items in the list. Each new item id should match the item id in the same position and be of the same product.
    payment_method_id: string! — The payment method id to pay or receive refund for the item price difference, such as 'gift_card_0000000' or 'credit_card_0000000'. These can be looked up from the user or order details.
- modify_pending_order_payment — Modify the payment method of a pending order. The agent needs to explain the modification detail and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed.
    order_id: string! — The order id, such as '#W0000000'. Be careful there is a '#' symbol at the beginning of the order id.
    payment_method_id: string! — The payment method id to pay or receive refund for the item price difference, such as 'gift_card_0000000' or 'credit_card_0000000'. These can be looked up from the user or order details.
- modify_user_address — Modify the default address of a user. The agent needs to explain the modification detail and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed.
    user_id: string! — The user id, such as 'sara_doe_496'.
    address1: string! — The first line of the address, such as '123 Main St'.
    address2: string! — The second line of the address, such as 'Apt 1' or ''.
    city: string! — The city, such as 'San Francisco'.
    state: string! — The state, such as 'CA'.
    country: string! — The country, such as 'USA'.
    zip: string! — The zip code, such as '12345'.
- return_delivered_order_items — Return some items of a delivered order.
    
    The order status will be changed to 'return requested'.
    The agent needs to explain the return detail and ask for explicit user confirmation (yes/no) to proceed.
    The user will receive follow-up email for how and where to return the item.
    order_id: string! — The order id, such as '#W0000000'. Be careful there is a '#' symbol at the beginning of the order id.
    item_ids: array! — The item ids to be returned, each such as '1008292230'. There could be duplicate items in the list.
    payment_method_id: string! — The payment method id to pay or receive refund for the item price difference, such as 'gift_card_0000000' or 'credit_card_0000000'. These can be looked up from the user or order details.
- transfer_to_human_agents — Transfer the user to a human agent, with a summary of the user's issue.
    
    Only transfer if
     -  the user explicitly asks for a human agent
     -  given the policy and the available tools, you cannot solve the user's issue.
    summary: string! — A summary of the user's issue.
telecom:
[AVAILABLE TOOLS]
- get_customer_by_phone — Finds a customer by their primary contact or line phone number.
    phone_number: string! — The phone number to search for.
- get_customer_by_id — Retrieves a customer directly by their unique ID.
    customer_id: string! — The unique identifier of the customer.
- get_customer_by_name — Searches for customers by name and DOB. May return multiple matches if names are similar,
    
    DOB helps disambiguate.
    full_name: string! — The full name of the customer.
    dob: string! — Date of birth for verification, in the format YYYY-MM-DD.
- get_details_by_id — Retrieves the details for a given ID.
    
    The ID must be a valid ID for a Customer, Line, Device, Bill, or Plan.
    id: string! — The ID of the object to retrieve.
- suspend_line — Suspends a specific line (max 6 months).
    
    Checks: Line status must be Active.
    Logic: Sets line status to Suspended, records suspension_start_date.
    customer_id: string! — ID of the customer who owns the line.
    line_id: string! — ID of the line to suspend.
    reason: string! — Reason for suspension.
- resume_line — Resumes a suspended line.
    
    Checks: Line status must be Suspended or Pending Activation.
    Logic: Sets line status to Active, clears suspension_start_date.
    customer_id: string! — ID of the customer who owns the line.
    line_id: string! — ID of the line to resume.
- get_bills_for_customer — Retrieves a list of the customer's bills, most recent first.
    customer_id: string! — ID of the customer.
    limit: integer — Maximum number of bills to return.
- send_payment_request — Sends a payment request to the customer for a specific bill.
    
    Checks:
        - Customer exists
        - Bill exists and belongs to the customer
        - No other bills are already awaiting payment for this customer
    Logic: Sets bill status to AWAITING_PAYMENT and notifies customer.
    Warning: This method does not check if the bill is already PAID.
    Always check the bill status before calling this method.
    customer_id: string! — ID of the customer who owns the bill.
    bill_id: string! — ID of the bill to send payment request for.
- get_data_usage — Retrieves current billing cycle data usage for a line, including data
    
    refueling amount, data limit, and cycle end date.
    customer_id: string! — ID of the customer who owns the line.
    line_id: string! — ID of the line to check usage for.
- enable_roaming — Enables international roaming on a line.
    customer_id: string! — ID of the customer who owns the line.
    line_id: string! — ID of the line to enable roaming for.
- disable_roaming — Disables international roaming on a line.
    customer_id: string! — ID of the customer who owns the line.
    line_id: string! — ID of the line to disable roaming for.
- transfer_to_human_agents — Transfer the user to a human agent, with a summary of the user's issue.
    
    Only transfer if
     -  the user explicitly asks for a human agent
     -  given the policy and the available tools, you cannot solve the user's issue.
    summary: string! — A summary of the user's issue.
- refuel_data — Refuels data for a specific line, adding to the customer's bill.
    
    Checks: Line status must be Active, Customer owns the line.
    Logic: Adds data to the line and charges customer based on the plan's refueling rate.
    customer_id: string! — ID of the customer who owns the line.
    line_id: string! — ID of the line to refuel data for.
    gb_amount: number! — Amount of data to add in gigabytes.
banking_knowledge:
[AVAILABLE TOOLS]
- KB_search_bm25 — Search the knowledge base using BM25 sparse retrieval.
    query: string! — The search query to find relevant documents.
    k: integer — Maximum number of documents to return (default 10).
- KB_search_dense — Search the knowledge base using dense embedding retrieval.
    query: string! — The search query to find relevant documents.
    k: integer — Maximum number of documents to return (default 10).
- grep — Search for a regex pattern in all knowledge base documents.
    
    Returns documents ranked by number of matches, with full content.
    pattern: string! — The regex pattern to search for (e.g., 'credit.*card', 'fee|charge')
- transfer_to_human_agents — Transfer the user to a human agent.
    
    The proper transfer reason enum can be found in the knowledge base: search it before calling this tool to select the proper applicable reason.
    summary: string! — A summary of the user's issue and what was attempted before transfer.
    reason: string [enum: fraud_or_security_concern|account_closure_request|deceased_account_holder|legal_or_regulatory_matter|account_ownership_dispute|complex_billing_dispute|abusive_customer_behavior|third_party_inquiry|technical_system_error|unconfirmed_external_communication|customer_demands_after_unavailable_offer_refusal|kb_search_unsuccessful_customer_requests_transfer|specialized_department_required|accessibility_or_special_needs|customer_frustrated_demands_human|supervisor_request_service_complaint|customer_requests_human_no_specific_reason|request_completed_customer_wants_human_followup|other] — The specific reason code for the transfer.
- get_current_time — Get the current time. Use this to get the current timestamp for logging verification records.
- get_user_information_by_id — Get the information (date of birth, email, phone number, address) for a user by their user id.
    user_id: string! — The ID of the user
- get_user_information_by_name — Get the information (date of birth, email, phone number, address) for a user by their name. Case Sensitive.
    customer_name: string! — The name of the user
- get_user_information_by_email — Get the information (date of birth, email, phone number, address) for a user by their email.
    email: string! — The email of the user
- change_user_email — Change the email address for a user.
    user_id: string! — The ID of the user whose email should be changed
    new_email: string! — The new email address to set for the user
- get_referrals_by_user — Get all referrals made by a user.
    user_id: string! — The ID of the user (referrer) to look up referrals for
- get_credit_card_transactions_by_user — Get all credit card transactions for a user.
    user_id: string! — The ID of the user to look up transactions for
- get_credit_card_accounts_by_user — Get all credit card accounts for a user.
    
    Returns information about each credit card account including card type,
    date opened, current balance, and reward points.
    user_id: string! — The ID of the user to look up credit card accounts for
- log_verification — Log a verification record after successfully verifying a user's identity.
    
    Call this tool after you have verified a user by confirming 2 out of 4 identity fields
    (date of birth, email, phone number, address). This creates an audit record of the verification.
    name: string! — The verified user's full name
    user_id: string! — The verified user's ID
    address: string! — The verified user's address
    email: string! — The verified user's email
    phone_number: string! — The verified user's phone number
    date_of_birth: string! — The verified user's date of birth (MM/DD/YYYY format)
    time_verified: string! — The timestamp of the verification (e.g., "2025-11-14 03:40:00 EST")
- give_discoverable_user_tool — Pass a tool to the user so they can execute it themselves.
    
    Use this when the knowledge base indicates that the user should perform
    an action themselves (e.g., "to do X, have the user call tool_name(args)").
    
    The user will then be able to call `call_discoverable_tool` with the same
    tool name and arguments to simulate executing the action.
    discoverable_tool_name: string! — The name of the discoverable tool (e.g., "open_webpage", "navigate_to_section")
    arguments: string — JSON string of arguments for the tool (e.g., '{"url": "https://example.com"}')
- unlock_discoverable_agent_tool — Unlock an agent discoverable tool that was found in the knowledge base.
    
    Use this when the knowledge base indicates that you have access to a specialized
    internal tool. The knowledge base will tell you the tool name to unlock.
    
    After unlocking, you can use the tool by calling `call_discoverable_agent_tool` with
    the tool name and required arguments.
    agent_tool_name: string! — The name of the agent discoverable tool to unlock (e.g., "calculate_apr_adjustment_7842")
- call_discoverable_agent_tool — Call an agent discoverable tool that you have previously unlocked.
    
    Use this after unlocking a tool with `unlock_discoverable_agent_tool`. The knowledge base
    will tell you which tool to use and what arguments to provide.
    agent_tool_name: string! — The name of the agent discoverable tool to call
    arguments: string — JSON string of arguments for the tool (e.g., '{"user_id": "abc123"}')
- list_discoverable_agent_tools — List all agent discoverable tools that you have called.
    
    Use this to see what specialized tools you have used.
